ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a wooden board A with mass $M=1\mathrm{kg}$ and length $L=1\mathrm{m}$ is at rest on a horizontal surface. The coefficient of kinetic friction between A and the horizontal surface is $\mu_{1}=0.1$. A iron block B with mass $m=1\mathrm{kg}$ (which can be treated as a point mass) is placed at the left end of A. The coefficient of kinetic friction between B and A is $\mu_{2}=0.3$. A horizontal constant force $F$ is applied to B. Take $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, and assume that the sliding friction equals the maximum static friction.

1. To maintain the uniform accelerated motion of A and B together, find the range of the force $F$.
2. If $F=3\mathrm{N}$, find the magnitude of the acceleration of A and the magnitude of the frictional force exerted by B on A.
3. If $F=5\mathrm{N}$, find the time it takes for the iron block to move to the right end of the wooden board. (You may express the answer in terms of radicals.)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, a long wooden board A is placed horizontally on a rough horizontal ground represented by diagonal-line shading; a small iron block B is placed above the left end of wooden board A; a horizontal arrow is drawn from B to the right, indicating that the external force F acts on B to the right. Take the rightward direction as the positive direction. Reasoning: Suppose that when A and B have no relative sliding and accelerate together, the acceleration is a, and the magnitude of the friction force between B and A is f. Because the external force F pulls B to the right, the friction force exerted on B by A is to the left; the friction force exerted by B on A is to the right; the friction force exerted by the ground on A is to the left. The normal pressure of the ground on A is equal to (M+m)g, therefore the magnitude of the ground friction force is μ1(M+m)g. Set up equations during common motion: for B, there is F - f = ma; for A, there is f - μ1(M+m)g = Ma. Substituting M=m=1 kg, μ1=0.1, g=10 m/s^2, the ground friction force is μ1(M+m)g=0.1×2×10=2 N. Adding the two equations gives F-2=(M+m)a=2a, so a=(F-2)/2. To make uniformly accelerated motion to the right, a>0 is needed, that is, F>2 N. Also from F-f=a, f=F-a=F-(F-2)/2=F/2+1. The maximum friction force between B and A is μ2mg=0.3×1×10=3 N, therefore it is required that f≤3 N, that is, F/2+1≤3, giving F≤4 N. Therefore the range for common uniformly accelerated motion is 2 N < F ≤ 4 N. When F=3 N, it still satisfies the above range. a=(3-2)/2=0.5 m/s^2; f=F-a=3-0.5=2.5 N. The friction force exerted by B on A and the friction force exerted by A on B are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, so the magnitude of the friction force exerted by B on A is 2.5 N, with direction to the right. When F=5 N, if the friction force required for common motion is F/2+1=3.5 N, it exceeds the maximum value 3 N, so B slides to the right relative to A. At this time the magnitude of the sliding friction force between B and A is f=μ2mg=3 N. For B: a_B=(F-f)/m=(5-3)/1=2 m/s^2. For A: a_A=(f-μ1(M+m)g)/M=(3-2)/1=1 m/s^2. The acceleration of B relative to A is a_B-a_A=1 m/s^2. Initially B is at the left end of A, and the relative velocity is 0; to reach the right end requires a relative displacement L=1 m, therefore 1=(1/2)(a_B-a_A)t^2=(1/2)t^2, solving gives t=√2 s.
